question.text: The minor arc AB and is denoted by $\overset{\frown}{AB}$.

answers.answer: The arc AB that lies inside angle AMB is the minor arc AB, written $\overset{\frown}{AB}$.
solution: The sides MA and MB of angle AMB cut the circle into two arcs.
The smaller arc, between A and B inside the angle, is the minor arc.
It is written $\overset{\frown}{AB}$.

checks.resolve_answer: The minor arc AB is the arc whose points lie inside angle AMB (the smaller arc, less than a semicircle); it is written $\overset{\frown}{AB}$.

question.text: The major arc ACB and is denoted by $\overset{\frown}{ACB}$.

answers.answer: The arc ACB that lies outside angle AMB, through point C, is the major arc ACB, written $\overset{\frown}{ACB}$.
solution: The sides of angle AMB cut the circle into two arcs.
The larger arc, passing through C, is the major arc.
It is written $\overset{\frown}{ACB}$ (three letters so it is not confused with the minor arc).

checks.resolve_answer: The major arc ACB is the larger arc, with its points inside the reflex angle AMB (outside angle AMB), more than a semicircle; it is written $\overset{\frown}{ACB}$ using a third point C.

question.text: What is the position of the points of arc AB with respect to angle AMB?

answers.answer: The points of arc AB lie inside angle AMB (in its interior, between its two sides).
solution: Arc AB is opposite to the central angle AMB.
Its points lie in the interior of angle AMB, between rays MA and MB.
So arc AB is the minor arc.

checks.resolve_answer: The points of arc AB lie in the interior of angle AMB (on the circle, between its sides).

question.text: What is the position of points of arc ACB with respect to reflected angle of angle AMB?

answers.answer: The points of arc ACB lie inside the reflex angle AMB, which is outside the angle AMB.
solution: Arc ACB is opposite to the central reflex angle AMB.
Its points lie in the interior of the reflex angle, outside angle AMB.
So arc ACB is the major arc.

checks.resolve_answer: The points of arc ACB lie in the interior of the reflex angle AMB, i.e. outside the (non-reflex) angle AMB.

question.text: If angle AMB is a straight angle, what do you notice?

answers.answer: AB is a diameter, and arc AB is congruent to arc ACB; each is a semicircle of measure 180°.
solution: If angle AMB is a straight angle, then A, M, B lie on one line.
So AB is a diameter of circle M.
Arc AB and arc ACB are congruent.
Each is called a semicircle, with measure 180°.

checks.resolve_answer: AB is a diameter, so arc AB and arc ACB are congruent; each is a semicircle with measure 180°.

question.text: Represent arcs AB and BC in the opposite figure.

answers.answer: Arc AB is the part of the circle from A (bottom) to B (lower right); arc BC is the part from B to C (right). They are adjacent arcs and together make arc ABC.
solution: Find the points A (bottom), B (lower right) and C (right) on the circle.
Trace the arc of the circle that goes from A to B and label it arc AB.
Trace the arc that goes on from B to C and label it arc BC (a different colour helps).
The arcs AB and BC meet only at B, so they are adjacent arcs.
Together they form arc ABC, so m(AB) + m(BC) = m(ABC) and m(AB) = m(ABC) − m(BC).

checks.resolve_answer: Circle M with points A, B, C in order; arc AB drawn from A to B and arc BC drawn from B to C, adjacent arcs sharing B, together forming arc ABC.

question.text: Is $\overset{\frown}{AB}$ congruent to $\overset{\frown}{EF}$? What do you deduce?

answers.answer: No, arc AB is not congruent to arc EF: they have equal measure (50°) but lie in circles of different radii, so arc EF is longer (twice the length of arc AB).
solution: The measure of each arc equals its central angle, so $m(\overset{\frown}{AB}) = m(\overset{\frown}{EF}) = 50^\circ$.
The circles are different (radii 7 cm and 14 cm), so the arcs have different lengths.
Length of $\overset{\frown}{AB}=\frac{50}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 7$.
Length of $\overset{\frown}{EF}=\frac{50}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14$, which is twice as long.
Deduction: equal measure gives equal length only in the same circle (or congruent circles), so the arcs are not congruent.

checks.resolve_answer: No. Arc AB and arc EF have equal measure (50°) but lie in circles of different radii (7 cm and 14 cm), so their lengths differ (EF is twice AB) and they are not congruent. Equal measure does not give equal length in different circles.
